entities.name: Diego de Ordaz
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Diego de Ordaz (c. 1480–1532) was a Spanish conquistador and explorer whose early endeavors in the New World significantly contributed to the mapping and subjugation of Mesoamerica and parts of South America. A pivotal figure in Hernán Cortés's conquest of the Aztec Empire, Ordaz distinguished himself through military prowess and an insatiable drive for discovery, most notably becoming the first European to ascend the active volcano Popocatépetl in 1519. His career spanned from the initial Spanish colonization efforts in Cuba to expeditions into the Venezuelan interior, emblematic of the era's relentless European expansion.

Ordaz arrived in the New World around 1509, initially serving under Diego Velázquez in the conquest of Cuba. By 1518, he had joined Hernán Cortés's expedition to Mexico, becoming one of his most trusted captains. During the arduous march to Tenochtitlan, Ordaz led a small party to the summit of Popocatépetl in October 1519, seeking sulfur for gunpowder—a daring feat that instilled both awe and fear in the indigenous populations and supplied a crucial resource for the Spanish campaign. He participated actively in the Noche Triste (June 1520) and the subsequent siege of Tenochtitlan (1521), enduring severe wounds but demonstrating unwavering loyalty and strategic acumen.

Following the fall of Tenochtitlan, Ordaz returned to Spain in 1522 to represent Cortés's interests and secure royal recognition for their achievements. Emperor Charles V rewarded him with a unique coat of arms featuring Popocatépetl and later granted him governorship of the province of Paria (present-day Venezuela) in 1525. Ordaz mounted an expedition to explore the Orinoco River in 1531, driven by rumors of El Dorado, but faced immense logistical challenges and conflicts with indigenous groups, ultimately failing to establish a lasting settlement or find significant gold. His explorations, however, provided early European geographical knowledge of the South American interior.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Diego de Ordaz was a significant early European explorer and conquistador whose daring ascent of Popocatépetl and crucial military service under Cortés contributed directly to the Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire and the expansion of the Spanish colonial project into Mesoamerica and parts of South America.
